source: Vér & Beranek 2e TABLE 14.1, PDF page 599 (printed p. 598)
about:
Seventeen commercial viscoelastic damping materials, from section 14.6 "Application of Damping Materials" of the chapter Eric E. Ungar and Jeffrey A. Zapfe wrote on structural damping. It is the only table in this catalogue where a loss factor carries the two things that decide it: the temperature at which the material reaches its greatest loss factor, and the frequency that temperature belongs to. Every other loss factor the library holds is a single number with neither, which is a property of a material only in the sense that a photograph is a property of a room.

The page is in degrees Fahrenheit and pounds per square inch, and the rows here are in degrees Celsius and pascals, so every one of those cells is marked as derived and says what the page printed. The book's own footnote offers "multiply tabulated values by 7 x 10^3" to reach N/m2; this catalogue does not use it, because a psi is 6894.757293 Pa by definition and the rounded factor is 1.5 per cent above it. The conversion of the temperatures is the page's own formula, which is exact.

These are not measurements this book made. Footnote a reads "Approximate values taken from curves in Ref. 11", so each number was read off a published curve, and the running text says of damping data in general that they should be obtained from the supplier. Three cells are corrupted in the printing and are registered in docs/ERRATA.md; they are held as misprinted and no number is served for them.
